Looking at this data, I matched Reisser and Eriksen records sharing identical dates and near-identical coordinates (within ~0.01–0.02°) across Australia/NZ/Pacific legs. These are not independent measurements: the triplicate station pattern, exact date matches, and tightly clustered ratios (dominant cluster ≈0.94, with secondary clusters at almost exact multiples of 2×, 3×, 4× and fractions of that same base value) indicate the two NCEI entries are built from the same underlying tows/cruises, just re-aggregated or re-processed differently (method field even flips between "Manta net" and "Neuston net" for the same station/date pair).

The median Reisser/Eriksen ratio across matched samples is about 1.04, but this reflects shared data (not independent confirmation)."}

answer.answer: The records share identical dates and near-identical coordinates for dozens of stations, with ratios clustering around 0.94 and its exact multiples (2x, 3x, 4x) rather than scattering randomly — a signature of the same underlying samples being re-aggregated/re-labeled across the two NCEI entries rather than independent re-sampling. The median Reisser/Eriksen ratio across matched samples is about 1.04, but this reflects shared data (not independent confirmation).
